sets.title: Authorization decision: normalization order vs config-driven rules variants
sets.description: The same resource-authorization decision in three semantically equivalent forms: carrier A uses the pristine guard-clause boolean-return form, carrier B checks conditions in a different normalization order (grant→role→owner instead of role→owner→grant) (sem_normalization_order variant), and carrier C uses configuration-driven rules with hardcoded config array (sem_config_driven variant). All three compute behaviorally identical results. No two carriers share a token run long enough for token/line tools to pair them, so only semantic detection is expected to recover the cluster.
sets.notes: SEM-11 variant (sem_normalization_order) uses different condition ordering. SEM-10 variant (sem_config_driven) uses hardcoded config array. Behavioral equivalence enforced by gen/seeds/access_guard/equivalence_test.php.

distractors.reason: near-miss: same auth vocabulary (user/resource/roles/grants/status) but computes a numeric trust score, not a boolean decision
